name: NICE Road (Bengaluru Peripheral Road + Link Road)
officialName: Bangalore-Mysore Infrastructure Corridor (BMIC) Project - Peripheral Road and Link Road

concession.modelName: Framework Agreement for an expressway, peripheral and link roads and townships, with toll and land-development rights
concession.operator: Nandi Infrastructure Corridor Enterprises Ltd (NICE), registered 16 Jan 1996
concession.tollEndCondition: Concession period of 30 years under clause 3.5.1 of the Framework Agreement, extendable by mutual consent (as stated by the State in the 2005 High Court case). The agreement itself has not been published.

timeline.title: MoU between Karnataka and a US-Indian consortium
timeline.description: The State Government signs a Memorandum of Understanding with a consortium of Vanasse Hangen Brustlin Inc. (USA), the Kalyani Group and SAB Engineering and Construction Inc. (USA) for the Bangalore-Mysore Infrastructure Corridor.

timeline.title: Nandi Infrastructure Corridor Enterprises registered
timeline.description: The project company is registered; the consortium members assign their rights to it on 9 Sep 1996.

timeline.title: Framework Agreement signed
timeline.description: Approved by the Government of Karnataka on 17 Mar 1997 and signed with Nandi on 3 Apr 1997. Schedule I lists about 20,193 acres for the project: 6,956 acres of government land and 13,237 acres of private land.

timeline.title: First challenge ends
timeline.description: A public-interest petition against the project (Somashekar Reddy, filed Nov 1997) is dismissed by the High Court on 21 Sep 1998; the Supreme Court dismisses the appeal on 26 Mar 1999.

timeline.title: High Court orders the State to implement the agreement
timeline.description: The Karnataka High Court dismisses one public-interest petition and allows two others, directing the State to execute the project as conceived and implement the Framework Agreement (as described by the Supreme Court in 2006).

timeline.title: Supreme Court upholds the Framework Agreement
timeline.description: The Supreme Court affirms the High Court, holding there was "neither fraud nor misrepresentation on the part of Nandi or any member of the Consortium".

timeline.title: House Committee report tabled in the Assembly
timeline.description: Tabled by Law and Parliamentary Affairs Minister T.B. Jayachandra. As reported, it recommends recovering Rs 1,350 crore of "illegal" toll collected by NICE since 2008, a high-level investigation by the CBI, CVC or Enforcement Directorate, and denotifying over 11,600 acres from acquisition; it says the company already has 605 acres more than it needs.

timeline.title: Supreme Court: no group housing at an interchange
timeline.description: The Supreme Court allows the appeals of the planning authority and the State, sets aside the High Court's 2019 judgment, and dismisses NICE's petitions over a group-housing scheme on 42 acres 30 guntas at interchanges 5/7 of the peripheral road (Kommaghatta), with liberty to approach the State under the Framework Agreement.

timeline.title: Cabinet sub-committee reviewing the agreement
timeline.description: PWD Minister Satish Jarkiholi tells the Legislative Council that a cabinet sub-committee headed by Home Minister G. Parameshwara is reviewing the agreement, toll policy and whether the agreement period is nearing completion, and that the government is considering removing tolls for two-wheelers.

analysis.summary: NICE Road is tolled under a Framework Agreement signed with the Government of Karnataka on 3 April 1997. The High Court in 2005 directed the State to implement the agreement, and the Supreme Court affirmed that in 2006. In December 2016 a House Committee report tabled in the Assembly recommended recovering Rs 1,350 crore of toll collected since 2008 and an investigation. In March 2026 the PWD Minister told the Legislative Council a cabinet sub-committee was reviewing the agreement.

reasonsStillTolled.text: Toll collection rests on the 1997 Framework Agreement, which the courts upheld: the High Court directed the State to implement it (2005) and the Supreme Court affirmed that (2006).
The concession period is 30 years under clause 3.5.1, extendable by mutual consent, according to the State in the 2005 High Court case.

The House Committee recommended recovering toll collected since 2008 (Dec 2016). As of March 2026 the State said a cabinet sub-committee was reviewing the agreement, toll policy and whether the agreement period is nearing completion.

openQuestions: What does the 1997 Framework Agreement say about toll rates, the toll period and termination if the expressway is not built?
What project cost has NICE claimed, and has it been independently audited?
How much toll has NICE collected each year since tolling began, per its audited accounts?
How much land was handed to NICE under the agreement, how much is in use for the roads, and how much was used for real estate?
What did the cabinet sub-committee recommend, and what did the government decide?

claims.text: NICE collected ₹4,756 crore in toll from 2008-09 to 2025, rising from ₹5.59 crore in 2008-09 to ₹735 crore in 2024-25, against an original project cost of ₹1,584 crore. He also said NICE earned ₹384 crore from land sales.
claims.claimedBy: H.D. Kumaraswamy, Union Minister, at a press conference in Bengaluru

amount.note: Toll collected 2008-09 to 2025, as claimed. The source of the figures was not stated.
